predecessors.name: Kampili Kingdom
predecessors.text: the Kampili enclave on the Tungabhadra around Hampi, the core of the new kingdom

predecessors.name: Hoysala Kingdom
predecessors.text: the Hoysala lands south of the Tungabhadra that Harihara I took over

successors.name: Bijapur Sultanate
successors.text: the Adil Shahi lands that took the north of the empire; the page lists the Sultanate of Bijapur as a successor

successors.name: Golconda Sultanate
successors.text: the Qutb Shahi lands of the east, a successor named in the infobox

successors.name: Kingdom of Mysore
successors.text: the Kingdom of Mysore, a successor named in the infobox; the Nayakas of Mysore, Keladi, Chitradurga, Gingee, Tanjore and Madurai became independent in the decline

ledger.x: 1336: Harihara I and Bukka Raya I found Vijayanagara.
1343: the Hoysala line ends and Harihara I takes its lands.
1347: Raichur fort goes to the Bahmanis.
1368: war with the Bahmanis over the Tungabhadra-Krishna doab begins.
1370: Vijayanagara attacks Madurai.
By 1374 Bukka Raya I wins the Tungabhadra-Krishna doab.
By 1374 the chiefdom of Arcot is defeated: 'By 1374 Bukka Raya I... defeated the chiefdom of Arcot, along with the Reddys of Kondavidu and the Sultan of Madurai.'
By 1374 Vijayanagara holds Goa: Harihara I 'gained Goa in the west by 1374'.
1378: Madurai becomes Vijayanagara's possession.
1378: the fighting over Madurai ends with the sultan's death at the battle of Madurai.
1407: treaty with the Bahmanis.
1417: the Bahmanis invade again.
1424: Kondavidu annexed.
1440s: Jaffna becomes a vassal.
1443: Alauddin Ahmad II defeats Deva Raya II, the last dated clash of the long Bahmani-Vijayanagara war; commemorated by the Chand Minar in 1445.
1446: the Gajapatis take the Tamil towns.

c. 1450: Kotte conquers Jaffna. 'The kingdom was overpowered by the rival Kotte kingdom around 1450' under Prince Sapumal; independence came in 1467. The page does not say when Vijayanagara's overlordship ended.
1453-54: Guntur and Kondavidu go to the Gajapatis.
1460: Udayagiri and Chandragiri fall.
1469: Mahmud Gawan invades.
c. 1470: pause. 'he temporarily allied his state with Vijayanagara around 1470.' The page does not say who held Kanchipuram afterwards.

c. 1472: Udayagiri and Chandragiri taken back. Purushottama Deva page (Varaha Purana): 'the General named Ishwara Nayaka captured the Udayagiri fort from the Gajapati forces stationed there'; the Vijayanagara page has Saluva Narasimha 'defeated the Gajapatis and held Udayagiri'. Neither page gives a year; 1472 is the…
February 1472: Goa goes to the Bahmanis.

c. 1476: Udayagiri and Chandragiri given back. After the second campaign, in which Purushottama 'imprisoned the Vijayanagara ruler', 'The Vijayanagara Emperor was freed in only the exchange of Udayagiri and Chandragiri regions back to Gajapati'. Mirror of…
1485: the Sangama dynasty gives way to the Saluvas.

c. 1485: the Tamil towns come back. [Repair 2026-10-24: the earlier event (coastal Andhra south of the Krishna, Chittoor, the two Arcots, Kolar, Kanchipuram, Tiruchirapalli, from the Gajapatis) misread the page.] The Vijayanagara page has Saluva Narasimha, as governor under Virupaksha Raya II…
1492: the Raichur doab leaves Vijayanagara's shape.
1503: the Saluvas give way to the Tuluvas.
1512: Krishnadevaraya takes the Raichur doab.
1512: siege of Udayagiri.
1514: the Gajapati lands fall to Krishnadevaraya: 'the subjugation of Odisha in 1514'; after Udayagiri 'The Gajapati army was then met at Kondaveedu' (undated).
1514: the war with the Gajapatis over Udayagiri ends in 'the subjugation of Odisha in 1514'.
19 May 1520: Raichur fort secured.
1520: the fight for the Raichur doab ends with the victory over Ismail Adil Shah.
After the war with Prataparudra the northern conquests go back: 'Krishnadevaraya returned all the lands that the Vijayanagara Empire had captured north of the Krishna River.'

c. 1521: about 193 cells go to Golconda in Cliopatria's 1521 step (lat 15.9-17.6 N, lon 77.8-82.3 E). The Krishnadevaraya page has the northern conquests returned ('returned all the lands that the Vijayanagara Empire had captured north of the Krishna River', no year) and the Quli Qutb Shah page, as read by the…
c. 1521: about 14 cells of Bidar's southern frontier. No page opened dates or explains it. Mirror of bidar-sultanate /ledger/2 (confidence 1).
1529: Cliopatria cuts the Madurai country out as the Nayaks of Madurai.
1530: Raichur and Mudgal lost.
1534: Cliopatria cuts the Thanjavur country out as the Nayaks of Thanjavur; same reading as Madurai (vassal until the decline).
1534: the doab retaken.

c. 1547: about 15 cells of the northern Kanara coast. Ibrahim Adil Shah I page: 'considerable acquisitions were made in the south along the west coast' and 'The farthest point of Bijapur territory now extended south of Goa'; no year (reign 1535-1558) and no…
1565: the capital moves to Penukonda.
After 1565 the nayakas become independent: 'Nayakas of Chitradurga, Keladi, Mysore, Gingee, Tanjore, and Madurai became independent' during the decline (undated); 1565 is a bridge.
After 1565 the Tanjore nayakas become independent (same sentence, undated).
1565: the Aravidu dynasty.
1565: the Raichur doab returns to Bijapur.
23 January 1565: the Deccan sultanates win at Talikota and take Hampi.
1565: the sultans leave.
1572: Mysore.
1572: Keladi.
1572: Chitradurga.
1572: Gingee.
1572: the rest of the 1564 shape is not drawn.
1575: the Carnatic goes to Bijapur.
1592: the capital moves to Chandragiri.
1604: the capital moves to Vellore.
1639: Madrasapatnam.
1646: the last remains of the empire end.

wars.name: Wars between Vijayanagara and the Bahmani Sultanate
wars.outcome: A long war over the Tungabhadra-Krishna doab: Bukka Raya I held it by 1374; Firuz Shah won in 1398 and 1406; a treaty of 1407 made Vijayanagara pay tribute; the Bahmanis invaded in 1417 and 1423 (siege of the capital) and Alauddin Ahmad II defeated Deva Raya…

wars.name: Vijayanagara conquest of the Madurai Sultanate
wars.outcome: Kumara Kampana destroyed the sultanate in 1370 (Bowman); the last sultan was killed at Madurai and Harihara II made it Vijayanagara's in 1378.

wars.name: Gajapati conquests of the Reddi and Vijayanagara east
wars.outcome: Kapilendra's forces failed in 1444, took Kondavidu in 1446 and crossed the Krishna after August 1453, holding Guntur by 1454; in 1460 Udayagiri and Chandragiri fell, and Hamvira Deva forced Mallikarjuna Raya to pay yearly tribute (undated).

wars.name: Mahmud Gawan's campaigns against Vijayanagara
wars.outcome: Kanjeeveram conquered in 1469, a temporary alliance around 1470, and Goa captured in February 1472 with the siege of Belgaum.

wars.name: Krishnadevaraya's campaigns in the Raichur doab and against the Gajapatis
wars.outcome: Raichur doab conquered 1512 and Raichur fort secured from Ismail Adil Shah on 19 May 1520; Udayagiri besieged 1512, 'subjugation of Odisha in 1514'; battle with Quli Qutb Shah at Pangal 1513; the northern conquests were returned.

wars.name: Wars with Bijapur over the Raichur doab
wars.outcome: Bijapur recovered Raichur and Mudgal in 1530, Vijayanagara seized the doab again in 1534, and it was returned to Bijapur after Talikota in 1565 (Adil Shahi page).

wars.name: Vijayanagara Civil War
wars.outcome: A succession conflict after Achyuta's death in June 1542; Salakaraju Tirumala invited the Bijapur sultan; Rama Raya's forces killed Salakaraju at the Battle of the Tungabhadra in 1543 and placed Sadasiva Raya on the throne.

wars.name: Battle of Talikota
wars.outcome: On 23 January 1565 the Deccan sultanates defeated Rama Raya, beheaded him and plundered the capital; the Aravidu court moved to Penukonda.

wars.name: Aravidu wars with Bijapur and others
wars.outcome: Continued wars, succession disputes and Nayaka rebellions wore down the remnant until it ended in 1646.

wars.name: Bijapur's Carnatic campaign
wars.outcome: Ali Adil Shah I 'annexed more land from Vijayanagara in a campaign which lasted until 1575', conquering Adoni and much of the Carnatic (Adil Shahi page).

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is recorded on any page opened.
